question: Judged on the printed per-task figures, because the record misreads P-79. Both papers discriminate stages of the MCI spectrum from controls in ADNI (EMCI vs NC, LMCI vs NC, LMCI vs EMCI, and NC/EMCI/LMCI three-class) with population-graph GCNs. The channel is MRI in both: P-14 fuses rs-fMRI with DTI, and P-79 fuses rs-fMRI with T1 gray-matter volume; the rule counts functional, diffusion and structural MRI as one channel. Cohort subsets (P-14's 184 subjects vs P-79's 436 ADNI2 subjects), architecture and validation (LOOCV vs stratified 5-fold) differ, which the rule allows.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy on the task-matched figures. The record's 'P-79: +8.5% vs baseline' is an average improvement over P-79's own baselines, not an accuracy, and P-14's 90.39% is the mean of three different binary tasks. The recorded gap (0.819) subtracts unlike quantities (condition 6).

figures.P-79: MCRSW-GCN, fused rs-fMRI+T1+phenotype, stratified 5-fold CV (ADNI2: 161 NC, 147 EMCI, 128 LMCI). Wilson intervals: NC vs EMCI 95.39% (n = 308) [0.924, 0.972], AUC 98.65; NC vs LMCI 97.44% (n = 289) [0.949, 0.987], AUC 99.75; EMCI vs LMCI 95.56% (n = 275) [0.924, 0.974], AUC 95.58; three-class 92.55% (n = 436) [0.897, 0.947], macro-AUC 98.96. fMRI+phenotype only (Scheme 2): 89.48% [0.856, 0.924]; 87.59% [0.833, 0.909]; 87.82% [0.834, 0.912]; 78.11% [0.740, 0.817]. Base model without its three modules (Ours1, fused input): 83.27% [0.787, 0.870]; 79.13% [0.741, 0.834]; 82.85% [0.780, 0.868]; 71.86% [0.675, 0.759]. Comparators on P-79's own NC vs EMCI data, fMRI+phenotype: HPGCN 84.73%, EV-GCN 83.54%, FCHGNN 84.45%, KMGCN 75.18%.

matched_figure_check: Matched figures exist and dissolve most of the gap. On the shared rs-fMRI-only input, which both papers report, three of four tasks agree within uncertainty in both directions. LMCI vs NC is 86.92% against 87.59%, LMCI vs EMCI 89.74% against 87.82%, and three-class 80.58% against 78.11%. EMCI vs NC differs (77.08% against 89.48%). For that task, and for the fused-model gaps, P-79's own data show the architecture is sufficient. On the same fused input, its base model without the three modules scores 83.27% on NC vs EMCI, which agrees with P-14's 85.42% in both directions, and its full model scores 95.39%. On fMRI input and P-79's own cohort, population-graph comparators span 75.18-84.73%, bracketing P-14's 77.08% (fMRI) and 85.42% (fused). As in C-40, a paper's own comparators on the same data reproducing the other paper's level is taken as showing the explanation sufficient, so condition 3 fails.
performance_validity: Borderline for P-79, and the verdict does not rest on it. Its fused results reach the threshold on internal 5-fold CV with no external MCI cohort (NC vs LMCI accuracy 97.44%, AUC 99.75; NC vs EMCI AUC 98.65; three-class macro-AUC 98.96). Its only external test is a depression dataset, not MCI. At 275-436 subjects per task the samples are moderate, and the rule does not fix what counts as small (compare C-84). P-14's highest figure (93.46%) is below 0.97.

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture, shown sufficient within P-79: its NRR, CW-STWNet and D-GAT modules raise binary accuracy from about 80% to above 95% on identical data.
candidate_explanations.quote: The baseline version (Ours1) achieves approximately 80% ACC in binary classification tasks, while the overall accuracy for the multi-class task remains below 72%.

candidate_explanations.difference: Fusion partner within the MRI channel: T1 gray-matter volume (P-79) against DTI structural connectivity (P-14).
candidate_explanations.quote: For convenient viewing, we use Ours (R), Ours (D), and Ours (F) to represent the proposed method with the R-fMRI, DTI and fused data as input, respectively.

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation and cohort subset: LOOCV on 184 subjects against stratified 5-fold CV on 436 ADNI2 subjects.
candidate_explanations.quote: We adopted stratified five-fold cross-validation to evaluate model performance.

reason: The record sets P-14's cross-task mean against P-79's improvement margin, which is not an accuracy (condition 6). On the task-matched printed accuracies, the fused-model gaps exceed uncertainty. But on the rs-fMRI-only input both papers report, three of four tasks agree. For the fourth (EMCI vs NC) and for the fused gaps, P-79's own base model and comparators on its data reproduce P-14's level (83.27% against 85.42%), so the paper shows the architecture is sufficient and condition 3 fails. P-79's fused figures are also near ceiling on internal validation (condition 5 borderline, not relied on).
